title: The Wrapper Stripe
logline: After nine years of rejected pitches, Lily finally gets all five friends to agree to her dream Halloween group costume: a box of crayons, hand-sewn, with a black headband for the wrapper stripe. Within a day, all four of them secretly defect at the same costume shop, each sure Lily will still have the other crayons, and the purple crayon arrives at the roof party alone.
coldOpen: Kids, for nine years your Aunt Lily begged us to wear a group costume, and for nine years we said no. In 2012, we finally said yes. That's when things got ugly.

couch.line: Wait. Is this the pumpkin story?
No. There is no pumpkin in this story. We don't talk about the pumpkin.

guests.name: Philippa
guests.role: Owner of Philippa's Costumes on Eighth Avenue for thirty-one years and judge of the roof party's costume contest. Has watched every group costume in Manhattan fall apart at her register and can predict each collapse to the minute.

guests.name: Hollis
guests.role: Marshall's new neighbor, a soft-spoken park ranger from Montana who says he has seen Bigfoot twice and is gently, devastatingly honest about everything.

guests.name: Josette
guests.role: The woman of Ted's Halloween fantasy, who recognizes his Le Corbusier costume on sight and finds his pedantry thrilling. She exists only in Ted's head.

scenes.summary: Two weeks before Halloween. Lily's tenth pitch: she isn't asking, she already sewed. A box of crayons, five colors assigned by personality, a black headband for the wrapper stripe. Everyone argues their color, Barney says purple alone is a grape, and they swear the crayon oath. Button: the box stayed intact until nine the next morning.

beats.line: Two weeks before Halloween, your Aunt Lily called an emergency meeting.
Okay. I've pitched a group costume nine years in a row, and you've said no nine years in a row.
And that streak is safe with me. No.
I pitched the Seven Dwarfs.
There are five of us.
I was going to be three of them.
So this year, I'm not asking. I already sewed them. Six weeks. I have a thimble callus.
Baby, you sewed? You don't even sew buttons. You staple them.
Five crayons. One box. Matching sweatsuits, and a black headband for the wrapper stripe.
One perfect photo. Framed, over our fireplace. Next to our wedding picture.
Next to it?
Above it.
Marshall, you're green.
Could I be Sasquatch Brown?
There's no Sasquatch Brown crayon.
Not with that attitude.
Robin, you're cerulean.
I'm not going to a party as something you catch in a hot tub.
Ted, you're burnt sienna.
Ooh. Fun fact, sienna is actually clay from Siena, in Tuscany. They roast it in kilns until—
That's why I gave it to you. So you'd say that tonight and never again.
Barney, you're goldenrod.
Goldenrod? Lily, I'm a closer. I'm gold.
You're goldenrod.
Goldenrod is gold that gave up.
And I'm purple.
Purple, all by itself? Lily, that's a grape.
That's what the wrapper stripe is for. It's the difference between a crayon and a grape.
Right hands up. Repeat after me. I solemnly swear to be a crayon.
I solemnly swear to be a crayon.
I solemnly swear to be goldenrod. God help me.
Nine years, baby. Nothing can stop us now.
Kids, the box of crayons stayed intact until roughly nine the next morning.

scenes.summary: Philippa's Costumes on Eighth Avenue. One by one, Ted (Le Corbusier, so the one will recognize him), Robin (bribing the contest judge for Rangers seats; sexy Mountie), Marshall (Bigfoot, to impress his ranger neighbor Hollis) and Barney (dressing as Ted for a play called The Mosby) defect, each sure Lily will still have the others. Philippa keeps count and gives the box until nine fifteen. Lily comes in for five headbands. Button: a free grape stem.

beats.line: The next morning, I went to Philippa's Costumes on Eighth Avenue. Just to look.
Hi. Hypothetically, if a man were already in a group costume—
You're leaving.
I'm not leaving. I'm going solo.
Honey, a group costume is a boy band. Somebody always goes solo. Usually the one with the hair.
Every Halloween I go up to that roof believing she's there. The one.
But nobody walks up to a crayon. A crayon comes in a box. A crayon is taken.
So I'm going as Le Corbusier. Round glasses, bow tie. The father of modern architecture.
Is that a cheese?
Nobody on that roof will get it. Except her. Whoever recognizes it, that's the one.
Oh my God. Le Corbusier. Villa Savoye, nineteen thirty-one.
You're the first person who's ever gotten it.
I've waited my whole life for a man who'd dress as a Swiss architect on purpose.
Technically, he became a French citizen in 1930.
Don't stop.
Besides, Lily will still have four crayons. Four is still a box.
Mm-hm. Glasses are aisle two.
Philippa. You're judging the costume contest on Ted's roof. I'm here to bribe you.
I don't take bribes. I take retail.
First prize is two seats behind the glass at the Rangers. You can hear the players swear. In French.
Crayons never win. Group costumes split the vote. So what wins?
Sexy anything. But I never reward it. I'm a feminist.
What about a sexy Mountie?
That's different. That's patriotic.
Lily will still have three crayons. Three is still a box.
That's two.
Hi! I'd like your finest Bigfoot.
We have a gorilla and a sad bear.
Ma'am, Bigfoot is neither. He's a North American hominid.
There's a new guy in our building. Hollis. A park ranger from Montana. He's seen Bigfoot. Twice.
We talked at the mailboxes for forty-five minutes. Lily and I have never had a forty-five minute mailbox.
He said if he ever saw Bigfoot again, he'd know him anywhere. Ma'am, I want to be known anywhere.
Also, I've been the back half of a horse four Halloweens in a row. Lily's always the front.
And Lily will still have Ted, Robin and Barney. Three's a box.
That's three.
Exactly! Three!
Philippa! The usual.
Sexy pirate.
Not this year. This year, I'm going as the most dangerous man on Halloween. A man who wants to talk about his feelings.
On Halloween, every woman wants a nice guy. For one night.
beats.title: The Mosby
lines: 3. Say the word actually about a cornice.
4. She thinks: finally, a nice guy.
5. Be exactly like every other guy.

beats.line: Your friend Ted was in here this morning. Brown tweed. Sad eyes.
Perfect. One tweed blazer, red cowboy boots, and a deep, unearned sense of destiny.
Don't worry about Lily. She'll still have four crayons.
That's four. Four crayons gone solo, out of a box of five. I give it till nine fifteen.
Huh. Good for them.
Hi! I need five black headbands. For the wrapper stripes.
Five.
Five crayons! Nine years, and this time nobody's backing out.
I'm throwing in a grape stem. No charge.
Why would I need a grape stem?
Call it a hunch.

scenes.summary: Halloween, nine sharp. Lily arrives first, in purple; Philippa calls her a grape and asks where the rest of her is. Ted arrives as Le Corbusier, Robin as a Mountie everyone reads as a sexy nutcracker, Barney as Ted (and he's the only one who recognizes Ted's costume). Marshall, last hope, arrives as Bigfoot; Hollis calls him a UPS guy and says Bigfoot's way taller. Lily hands over the crayons she brought anyway and goes off to be a grape. Button: Philippa was one minute off.

beats.line: Halloween. The roof party. Nine o'clock sharp, the purple crayon arrived first.
Philippa! You came!
Oh, look. A grape.
A crayon. The headband's the wrapper stripe.
Sure. Where's the rest of you?
Running late. Marshall went down for ice. He's green.
Is he.
Ted! There's my burnt sienna!
Lily, before you say anything—
Why are you dressed like a pharmacist at a funeral?
Lily, I'm Le Corbusier.
Is that a cheese?
That's what I said.
Fine. I still have three.
Sexy nutcracker. Bold.
I'm a Mountie! It's a Mountie! Look at the boots!
Lily, it's Rangers seats behind the glass. I'd sell you for less. I'd sell Ted for parking.
Okay. Two. I can work with two.
Hi. I'm Ted Mosby. Architect.
I do not sound like that.
You sound exactly like that.
And I don't wear a pocket square.
Ted, I'm committed to the role. I'm not an animal.
Barney! You swore on goldenrod!
And it's working too well. Two women told me about their fathers. One asked me to help her move. In March.
Oh, nice. Le Corbusier. Villa Savoye, nineteen thirty-one.
You recognized it.
Ted, I'm you. I read your whole bookshelf in the cab. Spoiler: the flat roof leaks.
So the only person on this roof who gets my costume is me.
Okay. It's fine. I still have Marshall. Marshall would never do this to me.
Marshall?
You were green twenty minutes ago!
I changed in the stairwell. Mrs. Kaplan from 2C saw everything. She's a believer now.
There's a ranger, he's seen Bigfoot twice, it's not a crush, it's professional, and he's right behind me.
Hey, neighbor. Cool. Are you a UPS guy?
I'm Bigfoot.
Oh. No. Bigfoot's way taller.
I'm six four.
He's like nine.
Nice grape.
Crayon.
I brought your crayons anyway. In case anybody changed their mind.
They'll fit. I measured all of you in your sleep.
I sleep with a knife.
I know. Yours took a month.
Have fun, everybody. I'll be over by the water tower. Being a grape.
Nine fourteen. I'm getting sloppy.

scenes.summary: Twenty minutes later. The four defectors put on whatever part of Lily's one-size crayons fit and walk over to her at the parapet, a box of half-crayons. Lily tells them about the Three Bears costume her dad never showed up for; Mickey was pitching Trick or Treaty in Cleveland. Ted says they look like a box somebody sat on; Lily says they look like a box in May. Philippa gives the contest to the man dressed as Ted Mosby, Barney gives Robin the seats, and when Hollis asks if Lily's a grape, four crayons answer.

beats.line: Kids, Lily had cut all five crayons from one pattern. Her size. So everyone wore the part that fit.
Lilypad?
Baby. Is that the green?
Only the top fit. From the waist down, I'm still at large.
Burnt sienna. I kept the glasses. I'm a crayon who's read things.
Cerulean on top. The Mounties keep the boots. It's the law.
I could only get the pants on. They're tight in a way I respect.
You all look terrible.
Lil. Why does this matter so much to you? Really?
When I was seven, my dad promised we'd go trick-or-treating as the Three Bears. My mom sewed the ears for a month.
He said he'd be home by six. I waited on the porch in my ears until nine.
Then I went by myself. And every single house asked the same thing. Where's the rest of you?
A group costume is the only picture that proves everybody showed up.
Where was he?
A board game convention in Cleveland. Pitching a game called Trick or Treaty.
Oh no. I've played Trick or Treaty. It's four hours, and you can only negotiate candy.
Lil, I'm sorry. We look like a box somebody sat on.
No. You look like a box in May.
By May, every box in my classroom looks like this. Broken, mixed up, wrong colors in the wrong slots.
A perfect box just means nobody's drawn anything yet.
So which one of us is the crayon that got chewed?
Baby.
Attention. The winner of this year's costume contest is the man dressed as Ted Mosby.
I'm right here!
And you're not nearly as convincing.
Barney. Those are my Rangers seats.
Take them. Take Lily. She's never heard a grown man swear in French.
Oh no. The Mosby is in my bloodstream.
Hey. Is your wife a grape?
She's a crayon!
Cool. Bigfoot's still way taller.
Let it go, Hollis!
Kids, every Halloween since, we've been a broken box of crayons. Uncle Barney still comes as me. He's won eleven years running. I've never placed.
